title: Surpassing Great the Gift of God
description: Surpassing Great the Gift of God in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sur-pass-ing great the gift of God To err-ing mor-tals given, A way that, from their dark a-bode, Leads to the light of heaven.

lines: Surpassing great the gift of God
To erring mortals given,
A way that, from their dark abode,
Leads to the light of heaven.
O Christ Who art the living way,
Plant Thou my feet therein,
And lead me lest I go astray
In luring paths of sin.
Too long I've found a sad delight
In wandering from Thy care,
Nor feared the sudden fall of night,
The darkness, and the snare.
O Jesus Christ, to Thee my soul
In conscious weakness clings;
Teach me to seek the kind control
That peace and safety brings.
And lead me upwards day by day,
Till, night and danger past,
I reach by Thee the living way,
The Father's house at last.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
